summary: A full-bleed row: a text column beside a framed media panel, mirrored by `alignment`.
useWhen: a marketing or overview section presents one thing with a screenshot beside it
a case-study or feature row on a landing or product page

useInstead.when: you are listing records with comparable fields
it is a short status message rather than a content section

headline.note: required — the heading is what makes this a section rather than a decorated div

actions.note: a secondary Button in the design

media.note: rendered inside the framed screen holder — pass the screenshot or embed itself, not the frame

left.use: media on the left, text on the right

right.use: media on the right — the variant names the media, not the text

guarantees: the headline renders as a real heading, so the card appears in the document outline
requires: `headingLevel` matching the surrounding outline — `h3` is the default because Figma applies Type/H3, but only the page knows the real level
notes: `h1` is deliberately not available: a full card is a section within a page, never the page's own title.

antiPatterns.why: an absent prop is the switch — Figma needs the boolean because an instance always holds every layer; React does not

antiPatterns.dont: leaving `headingLevel` at the default inside a section that is already at h3
antiPatterns.why: it produces a skipped or duplicated outline level

antiPatterns.dont: passing your own frame or border around `media`
antiPatterns.why: the component already draws the screen holder
